Entries.Text: Navigation
Navigation
This tool is only supported for Elden Ring.

Checks the navigation data of a loaded map: its NVA, its navmesh files (n, o and q), its ONAV, and the NVC files that connect it to its neighbours. Issues the vanilla game files also have are marked as inherited.

Select Validate to check this map.
Map
The loaded map to check.
The loaded map to check. Its neighbours are checked too where they are loaded; otherwise only this map's side of each NVC file is checked.
Actions
Check the map, or clear the results.
Validate

Reads the map's navmesh files, ONAV and NVC files if they haven't been read yet, and checks them. The vanilla data of the map is then checked in the background, to mark the issues the game files also have.
Clear
Clears the results.

View
Check

Draws a navmesh set of the map over the viewport: its faces coloured by their face data, its edges by what they connect to, its jump and ladder links, gate nodes and occlusion graph. Click faces to inspect them.
Overlay
What the overlay shows. It is drawn slightly above the navmesh, and can't be selected.
Show overlay

Draws the overlay of the map picked above. Reading a map's navmesh files the first time can take a moment. The Map Editor's own navmesh drawing can be hidden with the Navmesh render filter, which doesn't hide the overlay.
n set
The n navmeshes (n files, and the q files they are split into), the first half of the NVA's entries.
o set
The o navmeshes (o files), the second half of the NVA's entries. They usually have fewer faces; which characters use them is unknown.
Face opacity
How opaque the face fills are.
{0} user edges lead to a face that couldn't be found, and are drawn without an arc.
Layers
The parts of the overlay to draw, with the colour each is drawn in.
Faces
The faces, filled in a colour for each face data value. The legend below lists the values.
Inner edges
The edges between two faces of the same navmesh. Dense on large maps.
Open edges
Boundary edges that no connection joins to another navmesh.
Connected in the map
Boundary edges an NVA connector joins to another navmesh of this map.
Connected to a neighbour
Boundary edges an NVC file joins to a navmesh of a neighbouring map.
User edges
Jump, ladder and drop links: the edge, and an arc to the face it leads to.
Blocked user edges
User edges that also carry the blocked flag.
Gate nodes
The NVA's gate nodes, the points of the graph between navmeshes, as crosses.
ONAV areas
The ONAV's grid bounds, and a small box at each area's position.
ONAV links
Lines between the positions of linked ONAV areas.
ONAV cells
The grid cells each ONAV area covers. Heavy, and the order of the cell mask's bits is a guess: if the boxes don't line up with the areas, the guess is wrong.
Face Data
The face data values of the drawn faces, with the colour each is drawn in. What the bits mean is unknown.

Paint
Change the face data of faces by dragging over them in the viewport. Each stroke is one undo. Face data changes no indices, so connections stay valid; the map's save writes the navmesh files.
Paint face data in the viewport
While on, holding the picking button over the drawn set's faces paints them instead of selecting. Turns picking off.
Set

Add bits
Turn on the value's bits, keeping the faces' other bits.
Remove bits
Turn off the value's bits, keeping the faces' other bits.
The value to paint, in hexadecimal. The bits below, and the Use buttons of the legend, set it too.
A bit the drawn faces use. What it means in game is unknown.
Use
Paint this value.
The face's data in hexadecimal. Changing it is one undo.
Blocked
The user edge's blocked flag (EDGE_BLOCKED). Changing it is one undo.
The user edge's data in hexadecimal. What it means in game is unknown; the game files use values like 0x204 and 0x314. Changing it is one undo.
Impassable

No character can cross the face (eldenring.exe 0x1402E2A60). EMEVD 2003[13] adds or removes this bit at runtime on the faces of a node bank, by its entity ID, to block a path until an event flag is set.
High cost
Crossing the face costs 100 times as much in path finding (0x1402E1C70; not in sealed worlds).
Checked
Part of the bits that make the game check a character before it crosses the face, but no rule for it alone was found.
Lava
Only characters whose NpcThinkParam enables Lava navigation cross it, or at an extra cost those with a state the game sets at runtime (character +0xDCA0).
Ladder
Only characters whose NpcThinkParam enables Ladder navigation cross it.
Opens 0x10000
Lets characters cross a face with 0x10000. The game files never set it; it is added at runtime with the navmesh's dynamic face flags.
Gated (needs 0x8000)
No character crosses the face unless 0x8000 is also set, which happens at runtime: a face that something in game opens, such as a door.
Huge enemy area
Costs more, by a world setting, for characters that avoid huge enemies (NpcThinkParam isNoAvoidHugeEnemy off).
Opens 0x100000
Lets characters cross a face with 0x100000. The game files never set it; it is added at runtime with the navmesh's dynamic face flags.
Gated (needs 0x80000)
No character crosses the face unless 0x80000 is also set, which happens at runtime.
High cost
Crossing the face costs 100 times as much in path finding, on top of 0x8.
Character limit
Characters cross it only when a value of their physics (CSChrPhysicsModule +0x340, unnamed, starts at -90 degrees) isn't above a value of the navmesh. Only n faces use it.
Jump
A jump link, taken by characters whose NpcThinkParam enableJumpMove (enableJumpMove_onBattle in battle) allows it.
Fall
A drop link, taken by characters whose NpcThinkParam useFall_onNormalCaution (useFall_onSearchBattle in battle) allows it.
Extra cost
The link costs more: 4 for a jump, 2 for a fall.
